title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 89
paragraphs: In this struggle was slain the commander Ariabignes, son of Darius and brother of Xerxes, and many other notables of the Persians, Medes, and their allies were killed as well. Of the Greeks, on the other hand, only a few fell, for knowing how to swim, those whose ships were destroyed and who were not killed in hand-to-hand combat swam over to Salamis. But of the barbarians, most perished in the sea, not being able to swim. When the first ships turned to flight, then the largest numbers perished — for those stationed behind, trying to push their ships forward to the front so that they too might display some deed of valor for the king to see, crashed into ships of their own side that were fleeing.
